market_impact_summary.en: The stock market (S&P 500 +0.44%) shows a slight recovery, while the bond market (TLT -0.16%) records a slight decline. The US 10-year yield rises to 4.33% (+0.51%). Gold (GOLD +0.19%) and Bitcoin (-0.33%) show contrasting trends.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con risultati misti. Il Nikkei giapponese ha registrato un leggero aumento dello 0,03% a 53.430 punti, mentre lo Shanghai cinese ha guadagnato lo 0,26% a 3.890,16 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha invece subito una perdita dell'0,70% a 25.117 punti. Questi risultati lasciano un'atmosfera cauta in vista dell'apertura dei mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dello 0,44% a 6.611,83 punti. Il Dollar Index (DXY) ha guadagnato lo 0,05% a 100,03 punti. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, è salito del 3,76% a 25,08 punti. I tassi di interesse continuano a essere sotto attenzione: il tasso decennale USA è salito dello 0,51% a 4,33%, mentre il TLT Bond USA a 20 anni ha perso lo 0,16% a 86,65 punti. L'oro ha guadagnato lo 0,19% a 4.665,50 dollari l'oncia.

Sul fronte geopolitico, continuano le tensioni in varie parti del mondo. La situazione in Ucraina rimane critica, con implicazioni per i mercati energetici. L'Opek riunirà presto per discutere della produzione di petrolio, con potenziali impatti sui prezzi del Brent, che oggi guadagna l'1,61% a 111,54 dollari. La crisi energetica sta avendo effetti significativi su economie come quella del Regno Unito, dove pub e ristoranti stanno affrontando una 'perma-crisi'.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, gli investitori attendono con ansia i prossimi dati sul PIL degli Usa, che saranno rilasciati il 29 aprile. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse, con il tasso sui depositi al 2,00%. L'attenzione rimane alta sui dati economici in arrivo, come l'inflazione della zona euro, attesa per il 2 aprile. Il mercato continua a scontare le mosse delle banche centrali, con il tasso Fed Funds attualmente compreso tra il 3,50% e il 3,75%.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. La recente performance di prezzo ha visto BTC raggiungere brevemente i $70,000, influenzata dalle notizie geopolitiche e dalle dichiarazioni di Donald Trump sull'Iran. Dal punto di vista degli ETF, registriamo un afflusso netto giornaliero di $471.4M, segno di un interesse istituzionale ancora presente. Tecnicamente, Bitcoin si attesta a $68,615, con una leggera flessione del 0.75%.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum si quota a $2,104, con un calo dell'1.48%, mentre Solana scambia a $79.85, in ribasso del 2.40%. Binance Coin (BNB) si trova a $599.23, con una diminuzione dello 0.78%. Questi movimenti riflettono una generale tendenza ribassista nel mercato delle altcoin.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment, l'indice Fear & Greed si trova a 11, in territorio di Extreme Fear. Questo livello di paura estrema potrebbe indicare una possibile inversione di tendenza nel breve termine, ma è importante considerare anche i fattori macroeconomici. La correlazione con i mercati tradizionali resta significativa, e le recenti dichiarazioni della BCE e la prossima uscita dei dati macroeconomici potrebbero influenzare ulteriormente il mercato crypto.

In generale, il mercato crypto sembra essere in attesa di nuovi catalizzatori, sia dal fronte macroeconomico che dalle notizie specifiche del settore. La capacità di Bitcoin e delle altcoin di reagire ai flussi ETF e ai dati macro sarà cruciale per determinare la direzione futura dei prezzi.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, arrivederci alla prossima puntata.
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is cautious, with a risk-off mood prevailing in the markets. The VIX index is up 3.76% to 25.08, indicating increased volatility. This sentiment is reflected in the mixed performance of equities and safe-haven assets.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. The S&P 500 is up 0.44% to 6611.83, while the STOXX 600 is down 0.02% to 59.23. The Nikkei and Shanghai indices saw modest gains, while the Hang Seng declined 0.70%. In the currency markets, the EUR/USD pair is up 0.42% to 1.15, and the Dollar Index (DXY) is up 0.05% to 100.03. Commodities are mostly higher, with Brent crude up 1.61% to $111.54 and gold up 0.19% to $4665.50 per ounce. Bond yields are also moving, with the US 10Y yield up 0.51% to 4.33%, and the TLT Bond USA 20Y down 0.16% to 86.65.

On the macro front, attention is focused on the upcoming economic data releases. In the US, the PCE Core YoY is expected to provide insights into inflation trends. The Federal Reserve's stance on interest rates will also be closely watched. In the Eurozone, the CPI and unemployment data are due soon, which will help shape expectations around the European Central Bank's next move. Geopolitically, the situation in Ukraine and tensions in the Middle East continue to be closely monitored. The Bank of England is also grappling with the challenge of energy-induced inflation.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 
    Starting with Bitcoin, we see that the BTC ETF daily net inflow has been positive, with $471.4M flowing in. However, the price action has been muted, with BTC trading at $68,615, down 0.75% on the day. This comes as the Fear & Greed Index remains in extreme fear territory, with a reading of 11. 

    Moving on to altcoins, we see a sea of red, with ETH down 1.48% to $2,104, SOL down 2.40% to $79.85, and BNB down 0.78% to $599.23. The weakness in altcoins is not surprising given the uncertainty in the market.

    In terms of sentiment, the Fear & Greed Index is still in extreme fear territory, which could be a contrarian buy signal for some investors. However, it's essential to keep in mind that sentiment can shift quickly in the crypto markets. 
    Overall, it's a cautious approach for now, but the inflows into BTC ETFs are a positive sign for the long-term prospects of the space.

Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you tomorrow. A quick look ahead: keep an eye on market trends and we'll be back with more insights. Until then, goodnight and goodbye from Prais Alért.

articles.title: Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous
articles.snippet: In past wars, commanders worried about what would happen after crossing the line of departure. Today, the concern is whether they can cross it at all. Surely this is a concern as the United States considers sending a Marine expeditionary unit into the Persian Gulf. Before they enter, whether by air or sea, the fight will already be underway. Meanwhile, closed shipping routes are increasing the costs of shipping, America’s Gulf partners are under continued pressure, and the Houthis fired a missile to underscore the point. The path to the battlefield is the battlefield. No longer a prelude.This is by The post Iran’s Anti-Access and Area Denial Strategy Is Cruder Than China’s But Still Dangerous appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific
articles.snippet: During last summer’s 12-day war between Iran, Israel, and the United States, the U.S. military supported Israeli air and missile defense operations by utilizing its regionally deployed air and missile defense assets to intercept Iranian missiles and drones. By the time the shooting had stopped, CNN reported that the United States had expended 100 to 150 upper-tier, terminal-phase missile interceptors against Iranian missiles. This means that, in 12 days of fighting, the United States expended approximately 25 percent of its total stockpile — or 150 percent of annual global production at current production rates (though production increases are anticipated). The The post Closing the Air and Missile Defense Gap in the Indo-Pacific appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Pentagon-Linked REalloys Secures U.S. Rare Earth Supply Ahead of China Ban
articles.snippet: REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has signed an agreement to secure supply from one of the highest-grade rare earth deposits in the United States, with just nine months remaining before U.S. defense rules force the removal of Chinese material from the supply chain. The memorandum of understanding with U.S. Critical Materials Corp. gives REalloys access to up to 10% of production from the Sheep Creek project in Montana, with confirmed dysprosium, terbium, yttrium, and NdPr, the rare earth elements used in high-performance magnets for fighter aircraft, missile…

articles.title: Oil Supply Shock Ripples Through Fertilizer, Plastics, and Tech
articles.snippet: The worst supply shock in the history of the oil market is spilling over to critical supply chains, threatening shortages of medical supplies, fertilizers, semiconductors, and everyday consumer goods, including textiles, footwear, and cosmetics. When the Strait of Hormuz is shut, it’s not only Asian refiners scrambling for crude oil to turn into fuels. The naphtha, ammonia, urea, and helium supply that the Middle East would typically export via the most critical energy chokepoint is now trapped in the Persian Gulf. Petrochemicals producers…

articles.title: Rwanda Reaffirms Crypto Ban After Bybit Adds Franc Support
articles.snippet: Bitcoin Magazine Rwanda Reaffirms Crypto Ban After Bybit Adds Franc Support National Bank of Rwanda reaffirmed its ban on cryptocurrency use involving the Rwandan franc after Bybit introduced P2P trading support, warning of financial risks and lack of legal protections. This post Rwanda Reaffirms Crypto Ban After Bybit Adds Franc Support first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .
